question: Is the LG M50 discharge data used in big14-a-lgm50-validation and big14-a-lgm50-electrode-balance independent of the PyBaMM Chen2020 parameter set?
answer: NO for C/2, 1C and 1.5C: these curves are the tuning data of Chen2020. C/10 is not named in the tuning.

source.paper: C.-H. Chen, F. Brosa Planella, K. O'Regan, D. Gastol, W. D. Widanage, E. Kendrick, J. Electrochem. Soc. 167 (2020) 080534
source.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (the earlier registrations recorded the dataset licence CC-BY-4.0; the paper's licence differs and is recorded here)
source.how_read: full article text (HTML, open access) read in a browser on 2026-09-28; the PDF endpoints returned bot-detection pages and were not bypassed; nothing was downloaded or vendored
sections_read: Table IX and the text around it

facts_from_the_paper.validation_protocol: three cells, chamber at 25 degC, C/3 CC-CV charge, CC discharge at C/2, 1C and 1.5C between 2.5 and 4.2 V, each followed by a 2 h rest; this matches the Zenodo 4032561 files
facts_from_the_paper.tuning: eight parameters were adjusted by trial and error against these discharge curves: both particle diffusivities, both maximum concentrations, the positive-electrode 100 % SOC stoichiometry, and the three Bruggeman coefficients (the latter set to the theoretical 1.5 rather than tuned)
facts_from_the_paper.tuned_on: the 1C discharge first; the negative-electrode diffusivity was then re-adjusted separately for C/2 and 1.5C
facts_from_the_paper.C/10: not named in the validation protocol or in the tuning

checked_against_the_installed_library.how: pybamm.ParameterValues('Chen2020') in the WSL battery env (PyBaMM 26.8.0.0), 2026-09-28
checked_against_the_installed_library.result: PyBaMM ships the 1C-tuned column: negative diffusivity 3.3e-14, positive 4e-15, maximum concentrations 33133 / 63104, initial positive stoichiometry 0.26999, Bruggeman 1.5

consequences: big14-a-lgm50-validation and big14-a-lgm50-electrode-balance: their C/2, 1C and 1.5C comparisons are consistency with the parameterisation's own tuning data, not independent validation. Their pre-registered outcomes (both NOT MET) stand; a model that misses its own tuning data is a stronger negative, not a weaker one.
any future MET on these curves is an in-sample result and likely optimistic; the out-of-sample model-form error stays UNKNOWN until independent LG M50 data is used
PyBaMM's Chen2020 negative diffusivity is the 1C value; the authors themselves needed a 2.5x smaller value at C/2, the rate flagship A runs
the C/10 curves are the only ones outside Chen2020's tuning; big14-a-lgm50-electrode-balance already used cell02 C/10 for calibration
